title: Understanding R-squared: Evaluating Goodness of Fit in Regression Models

cues.en: Instructor: Hello and welcome back.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回來。

cues.en: Today, we're talking about the R squared, a very important concept when it comes to evaluating the goodness of fit of our models.
cues.zh: 今天介紹 R²，評估模型擬合優度時非常重要的概念。

cues.en: Now, in order to understand R squared, we're going to need to look at two versions of our chart.
cues.zh: 要理解 R²，先看兩個版本的圖。

cues.en: So here is our data set, and what we're going to do here is plot the regression as we were doing before.
cues.zh: 這是資料集，我們和之前一樣畫出迴歸線。

cues.en: And here's our data set, again, and this time we're going to just plot an average line, and we'll see that in a second.
cues.zh: 這裡是相同資料，但這次只畫平均值的水平線，稍後會看到。

cues.en: So we'll start with the regression.
cues.zh: 先從迴歸開始。

cues.en: Let's draw our regression line.
cues.zh: 畫出迴歸線。

cues.en: As usual, let's project vertically our data points onto it.
cues.zh: 一樣將資料點垂直投影到線上。

cues.en: And for each data point, we're going to look at the difference between yi, the actual value, and yi hat, the predicted value.
cues.zh: 對每個點，觀察實際值 yi 和預測值 ŷi 的差。

cues.en: Now as we discussed before, the way we built this line is we are minimizing this sum over here, and that is the ordinary least squares method.
cues.zh: 如前所述，建立這條線時，最小化這裡的總和，這就是普通最小平方法。

cues.en: Well, actually this sum has a name, it's called the residual sum of squares, and it's indicated by this abbreviation.
cues.zh: 這個總和有名稱，叫殘差平方和，用這個縮寫表示。

cues.en: Now on the right here, we're going to draw an average line, and this is simply taking all of the y values,
cues.zh: 右邊則畫平均線，也就是取全部 y 值，

cues.en: So the actual values of our data set, the y values, and taking their average.
cues.zh: 取資料集實際 y 值的平均。

cues.en: Again, we're going to project vertically our data points onto this line.
cues.zh: 一樣將資料點垂直投影到這條線。

cues.en: And for each data point, we're going to look at yi.
cues.zh: 對每個點，看 yi。

cues.en: And here we're going to calculate another total.
cues.zh: 這裡再計算另一個總和。

cues.en: And this one is called the total sum of squares, and is indicated by this abbreviation.
cues.zh: 稱為總平方和，用這個縮寫表示。

cues.en: And it's similar to the residual sum squares, but instead of using yi hat, we're looking at the difference between yi, the actual value,
cues.zh: 和殘差平方和類似，但不用 ŷi，而是看實際值 yi，

cues.en: and y average, the average value of our data set.
cues.zh: 與資料集平均值 ȳ 的差。

cues.en: And now we can calculate R squared.
cues.zh: 現在可以計算 R²。

cues.en: R squared is defined as one minus the ratio between the residual sum squares and the total sum of squares.
cues.zh: R² 定義為 1 減去殘差平方和除以總平方和的比值。

cues.en: Now, let's pause here for a second and discuss this a bit.
cues.zh: 先停一下，討論這件事。

cues.en: So we know that we're minimizing the residual sum squares.
cues.zh: 我們知道，要最小化殘差平方和。

cues.en: We wanna make it as small as possible.
cues.zh: 希望它越小越好。

cues.en: And from these two images, you can already see just by judging based on the lengths of these blue dotted,
cues.zh: 從兩張圖中，只要比較藍色虛線的長度，

cues.en: blue dashed lines, we can see that they're generally longer on the right where the average is and they're shorter where the regression is.
cues.zh: 就能看到右邊平均線的距離通常較長，左邊迴歸線的較短。

cues.en: And that's because we've designed our line to minimize these lengths, so the sum squared is smaller.
cues.zh: 因為我們設計迴歸線，就是為了將這些距離的平方和最小化。

cues.en: And so what that means is that the residual sum squares is usually, in most cases, it's less than the total sum of squares.
cues.zh: 所以大部分情況下，殘差平方和小於總平方和。

cues.en: So the way to think about it is in the total sum squares on the right, you're just putting an average line, you're not modeling anything.
cues.zh: 右邊只是放一條平均線，沒有真正建立模型。

cues.en: This is the most rudimentary thing that we can do is just put our average line and approximate our data with that average line.
cues.zh: 這是最基本的做法，以平均線近似資料。

cues.en: Of course, it will be, and it should be worse than any thought out model that we create, which is the example on the left.
cues.zh: 理論上，它應該比左邊這種經過設計的模型更差。

cues.en: So thereby, unless our regression model is facing absolutely the wrong way, for example, a downward slope on the left over here,
cues.zh: 除非模型完全朝錯誤方向，例如左邊若是向下傾斜，

cues.en: if our model was sloping downwards, then the residual sum of squares would be huge because our model's just incorrect.
cues.zh: 殘差平方和會非常大，因為模型根本不正確。

cues.en: But in all other cases the residual sum of squares is less than the total sum squares.
cues.zh: 其他情況下，殘差平方和小於總平方和。

cues.en: And what that means is that the ratio is less than one.
cues.zh: 因此比值小於 1。

cues.en: So R squared is somewhere between zero and one.
cues.zh: 所以 R² 位於 0 到 1 之間。

cues.en: And the better our model fits the data, the smaller the residual sum of squares will be, and that means the greater R squared will be.
cues.zh: 模型越貼近資料，殘差平方和越小，R² 也就越大。

cues.en: So here's a quick rule of thumb for R squared.
cues.zh: 以下是 R² 的簡易判斷準則。

cues.en: Now bear in mind that it highly depends on the context, and this rule of thumb is just for the practical tutorials that we're looking at in this section of the course.
cues.zh: 但請記住，它非常依賴情境，這些準則只針對本章的實作教學。

cues.en: And here we go.
cues.zh: 看看吧。

cues.en: So if you have a one, R squared of one, that's a perfect fit.
cues.zh: R²=1，代表完美擬合。

cues.en: That means there residual sum squares is zero, and basically your line is going through all the data points, which is virtually impossible.
cues.zh: 殘差平方和為 0，曲線通過所有資料點，這幾乎不可能。

cues.en: So it's very suspicious.
cues.zh: 所以會讓人懷疑。

cues.en: If your R squared is about 0.9, that's a very good model.
cues.zh: R² 約 0.9，代表很好的模型。

cues.en: If your R squared is less than 0.7, it's not a great model.
cues.zh: 低於 0.7，就不算太好。

cues.en: It's not the end of the world, but not great.
cues.zh: 不是完全不能用，但不出色。

cues.en: If it's less than 0.4, that's quite a terrible model.
cues.zh: 低於 0.4，是相當差的模型。

cues.en: And if it's less than zero, then the model makes no sense for this data as we discussed.
cues.zh: 若小於 0，正如剛才所說，模型對這份資料沒有意義。

cues.en: So there we go, that's how the R squared works.
cues.zh: 這就是 R² 的運作方式。

cues.en: A very important concept to understand because it's used quite a lot to evaluate models.
cues.zh: 這個概念很重要，因為經常用來評估模型。

cues.en: I look forward to seeing you next time.
cues.zh: 期待下次見到你。

cues.en: And until then, enjoy machine learning.
cues.zh: 在此之前，享受機器學習吧。
